description.narrative: In April and May 2022, the Province of Kwa-Zulu Natal (South Africa) experienced heavy rainfall, resulting in the deaths of over 400 people and severe damages to (business) property, electricity, sanitation and public infrastructure. The impact on the South Durban Basin (SDB) has been particularly severe. The SDB is the second most concentrated industrial area in South Africa and makes a material contribution to regional supply chains across sub-Saharan Africa. To prevent further (future) damages to this basin, the Municipality of eThekwini sent out an official request to the Dutch Disaster Risk Reduction & Surge Support (DRRS) programme for technical support to assist the city of Durban with a flood risk assessment and advice on flood risk mitigation measures. The Government of The Netherlands has since implemented three actions: 1) A brief desk study to determine the potential added value of a DRRS-Team in supporting the development of a comprehensive flood resilience strategy for the Prospecton area, 2) A full economic flood risk assessment of the Prospecton area that functions as a starting point for the development of a flood resilience strategy and 3) Deployment of a DRRS-Team of experts with the objective to develop a roadmap to achieve a comprehensive flood resilience strategy for the Prospecton area in the South Durban Basin.The objective of this DRRS assignment is to follow up on the work undertaken to support the Municipality of eThekwini on flood risk mitigation with the aim to advance the recommendations given in the report.
